report.clinical_summary: The patient has been diagnosed with Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL) in early stage and is on medication that they believe is important for managing the disease. They experience significant functional impairment - can barely get out of bed, missing work, unable to concentrate, and small tasks feel overwhelming. They have developed constant pressure-type headaches starting about a week after beginning medication, which they haven't mentioned to their hematologist due to fear of being a burden. They also experience severe fatigue that feels different from normal tiredness. They view CLL as a chronic condition they will 'always be managing' and attribute it to genetics (father had it). Their emotional response is described as a 'rollercoaster' between optimism and feeling overwhelmed/down. They feel limited personal control ('no say in any of it') and have significant concerns about medication side effects and long-term efficacy. They rely on routine and family support for coping.
